title: fix: use static supporter logos
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replaces runtime-generated supporter artwork with 21 static provider SVG logos ported from the website v2 work.
- Expands the Community page supporter list from 11 to 21 providers and tightens the responsive grid.
- Removes the orphaned supporter image generator, image API defaults, prompt configuration, and stale README guidance.
- Fixes inconsistent branding and avoids unnecessary generation API requests whenever the supporter section loads.
- Validated with Biome, `git diff --check`, `npm run build`, and desktop/mobile browser checks confirming all 21 assets render.

gist.headline: The logos stopped improvising
gist.blurb: The Community page traded generated supporter art for the real thing: 21 crisp provider logos, neatly planted in a tighter grid. Fewer API requests, less brand jazz improvisation.
gist.summary: The Community page now uses 21 static SVG logos for supporters—including AWS, Cloudflare, NVIDIA, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Replicate, and more—instead of runtime-generated artwork, with a tighter responsive grid and the old image generator removed.
gist.impact: Visitors get consistent, correctly branded supporter logos across desktop and mobile while the page avoids generation API requests just to render the supporter section.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful community gardener replacing a wobbly magic image-making machine with a tidy garden wall of 21 small, recognizable-but-simplified provider logo plaques. The static logo tiles should be arranged in a responsive-looking trellis grid, with a few flowers and code-plants growing around it to show that the community support network is stable and flourishing.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute yellow-and-dark-brown striped bee mascot with black oval eyes, pink rectangular blush cheeks, a happy smile, light blue rounded wings, and a tiny gardener apron, carefully hanging neat SVG-style supporter logo plaques on a lime green (#ecf874) trellis beside a retired little image-generator machine. Small flowers, vines, and code-plants grow around a tidy grid of 21 logo tiles; cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with dark purple (#110518) outlines and subtle CRT glow.
